items.title: Sammy Penn Interview, 1960-04-21
items.q: But at the time I did hear him, he had a good band.

ctx.x: I was going to ask if you could talk a minute about the Sam Morgan band. Did you hear that? What type band was that? I never got to hear them. They did make a couple of records.

Well Sam Morgan had a nice band. Sam Morgan and Celestine used to be the two of the best bands you had around here once. In fact I didn't hear him too much because after he died his brother taking it up. Well then they left and it was always over the lake somewhere. But at the time I did hear him, he had a good band. That's all you could hear them days was Sam Morgan and Celestine. They really had a nice band. Did you ever hear them play?

No, I never have. Never have played them. Somebody told me that Sam Morgan was about the first one or at least a lot of times he used to use a slapstick such as Manuel and Kid Thomas use quite often today. I wonder, did you ever play the slapstick too, Sammy?

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1964-03-21
items.q: And Morgan, I went out with Morgan on the lake. I played with Morgan out there.

ctx.x: Well. No. Sammy Penn. Only chance Sammy Penn got. He was on his own. Because I'm a good boy.

Fall off. Yeah. Okay. When were you born? I was born in September. September the 15th. 1902. And where? In Morgan City, Louisiana. And did you play any music out there at all? That's where I started at. I started playing in Morgan City. When I started playing music. It's a funny thing to tell you. What I'm going to tell you. I started. I had one of those cheese boxes. For snare drum. And a white tub. They call it. For a bass drum. And a fellow made me some springs. For a pedal. Made a pedal. That's how I started…
